result.title: Speculative Sampling in Interactive Video Generation
result.summary: Interactive video generation commonly relies on small bidirectional chunks to reduce response latency. Yet our preliminary experiments show that larger chunks improve video quality and better utilize GPU parallelism, allowing more latents to be sampled with only a modest increase in sampling time. Motivated by these observations, we propose Speculative Sampling, a strategy that combines the modeling power of large bidirectional windows with the low-latency interaction of small ones. It expands the modeling window by appending noise latents as padding and caches the resulting predictions for reuse when the condition remains unchanged. Predictions are delivered incrementally, while the uncommitted future remains replaceable. Our latency analysis shows that this removes the waiting-time lower bound imposed by chunk boundaries, shifting the optimization focus from reducing chunk size to accelerating per-chunk sampling. Bidirectional window size thus becomes a decision variable for jointly optimizing visual quality and sampling time, rather than a necessary constraint on low-latency interaction. This opens a path to serving large bidirectional models in interactive streaming systems without complex streaming post-training.

AI.brief_summary: 论文研究交互式视频生成中的延迟问题，提出 Speculative Sampling：用噪声 latent 作填充扩大双向建模窗口，缓存预测并在条件不变时复用，从而增量交付预测、保留未提交未来的可替换性。
AI.relevance_reason: 「缓存 latent 预测＋增量提交＋未提交未来可替换」的机制可能与 LVR 中候选 latent 状态的推测式生成、提交/回滚及条件不变时的缓存一致性有可供核查的线索，但原文属视频生成领域，能否迁移到多模态推理状态仍需核查。
